correctness.rationale: For n≥4 the threshold is equivalent to connectedness of every induced four-vertex graph: a disconnected four-set gives an (n−4)-deletion, and any disconnecting deletion of at most that size leaves a four-set meeting two components. The complement consequently forbids K₁,₃ and K₂,₂ as subgraphs. Maximum degree two and the absence of induced cycles of length at least five in inversion graphs give exactly paths and triangles. Value complementation sends noninversions to inversions, and inversion components are direct-sum blocks. The known path block multiplicities and the single triangle block give precisely the weighted block sum; ordered concatenation gives the reciprocal formula. The three-vertex test at the next threshold reduces the complement to a matching and therefore gives the Fibonacci cumulative count, with the complete inversion graph represented just once. In the repaired statement the exact OEIS overlap is now proved: if l_i and r_i count left and right inversions incident with i, then the degree is their sum and displacement their difference. Under displacement ≤2, simultaneous l_i,r_i>0 forces σ(i)=i, at most one contributor on either side; otherwise the degree equals absolute displacement. Under this degree bound, four-cycles are induced and correspond exactly to 3412. The displacement bound also forces any occurrence to be on four consecutive positions and values, so the OEIS description by swapping adjacent pairs has no convention gap. The independent bounded OEIS-class comparison through order eight corroborates the identification; the all-order conclusion is analytic. The supplied verifier was inspected, not run; its replay from the frozen package remains unchanged.
